title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance director says DLSS 5 does right by KCD 2, 'people are crazy' for thinking it's AI slop
summary: "I am the creative director of the game. This is our original artistic vision."
body: DLSS 5 is a controversial technology for all sorts of reasons —you might have heard about this little thing called AI slop—but perhaps the most infamous is its uncanny look . Real concerns have been raised about the potential for something so aesthetically transformative to preserve a game developer's artistic intent, with Nvidia trying to run interference on this very point. Director of both Kingdom Come: Deliverance games, Daniel Vávra, has re-entered this battle on the side of DLSS 5. Last Sunday, he took to X to say that some critics of the tech have "literally gone crazy," providing a before-and-after comparison with KCD 2 to say that it indeed helped realize the team's vision. title: After a massive 2021 office expansion, Bungie is now trying to sublease its 211,000 square foot headquarters
summary: Bungie says it "will continue to maintain a physical office presence in Bellevue."
body: In 2021, as studio CEO Pete Parsons cited the company's recent "tremendous growth and opportunity," Bungie announced its plans for a massive expansion to its Bellevue, Washington headquarters . The campus embiggening, which internal sources have reportedly described as costing "hundreds of millions" of dollars, more than doubled the size of Bungie's offices from 84,000 square feet to just under 211,000. Now, after five and a half years of spending sprees, publisher acquisitions, stumbling product launches, project cancellations, and repeated mass layoffs, Bungie appears to be seeking subletters for the goliath game development headquarters it's no longer capable of filling. According to a 10-page leasing brochure reviewed by The Game Post , Bungie is seeking interested renters to sublease its expansive headquarters, listing its 210,984 square feet as a "turn-key" production facility. In addition to expected office fixtures, the listing also features a dedicated lobby, gym and exercise facilities (including a rock climbing wall), a motion-capture studio, a cafe, catering space, and a private exterior patio. title: A popular streamer turned down a 6-figure deal to play Arc Raiders because 'the game frustrated me so much'
summary: Seven-figures? Now we're talking.
body: Everyone has a price. Maybe it's $100, maybe it's $1,000, maybe it's for someone to see your innate value as a human being, or maybe it's $1,000,000. Popular streamer TimTheTatman recently revealed what it would take to get him to go back to Arc Raiders , and spoilers, it's not the third option. There was apparently an ad deal floating around for the Arc Raiders and Subway collab, which TimTheTatman was approached for, but did not entertain. "I did say no to six-figures with Arc Raiders, I did," he revealed in a stream earlier this week. "I said 'No thank you'. And it was the Subway Arc Raiders ad. I said I just can't do it, I'm sorry." (Image credit: Embark) This was met with the exact response you'd expect with people being baffled that he'd ever think of turning down such a lucrative offer. "That's kind of the funny part of being in a streamer position," TimTheTatman continued. "People say 'you're a fucking sellout' but then in the same breath I said I passed on six-figures from Arc Raiders and people are like 'you're fucking stupid'." title: Great, now motherboard prices might be next to spike thanks to component costs increasing by up to 50%
summary: PC gaming sure ain't cheap.
body: PC gaming has always been an expensive hobby, but prices have become downright ridiculous as of late. It's bad enough that Nvidia's RTX 50-series cards cost slightly less than an international flight , but the memory supply crisis is also driving up the price of RAM and SSDs . Now it looks like motherboards might be next to see a significant price spike. Board Channels is a forum for hardware manufacturers and partners to communicate. One poster recently wrote , "The price of upstream raw materials for motherboards has indeed risen significantly." They go on to say that the price of motherboard PCBs alone has increased by between 15% and 50% . Wi-Fi modules are said to have gone up between 10% and 20%, while capacitor prices have also gone up approximately 50% (via Videocardz ). As we've reported before, these price increases are likely caused by material shortages resulting from the Strait of Hormuz crisis and the ongoing Iran war . For instance, PPE resin can be thought of as the glue that binds the many layers of a PCB together, and a huge chunk of the world's high-quality PPE comes from petrochemical company Saudi Basic Industries Corporation (SABIC) in Saudi Arabia. title: In a sea of failed live service games, I'm shocked to see someone trying to make a MOBA
summary: Project Zeta is trying to crack a near-impenetrable market.
body: Making a live service game these days feels like trying to shoot an arrow at a flea while blindfolded. Striking gold with a hot new shooter or other team-based multiplayer game with a quirky twist seems like an exercise in futility, but that isn't stopping developers and publishers from trying to be the next big thing. Personally, if I was trying to enter an already-volatile market, I'd probably be steering well clear of MOBAs. They're finicky, have a high barrier to entry, and require a ridiculous amount of time commitment to ever be remotely good at them. Even then, dragging a League or Dota player away from their game to try another one is a big ask. Hell, I'm still shocked Deadlock has managed to do it. (Image credit: Krafton) So I don't know whether to applaud developer Nirvanana for giving it a go with Project Zeta, or grab the team by the shoulders and give them a good old shake for doing something I perceive to be utterly reckless. Though, as Nirvanana will maintain, Project Zeta isn't quite a MOBA. As the developer tells me, it's actually a 4v4 multi-team tactical arena battle. Not battle royale, just battle. "We tried not to be tied down to those traditional things," Nir…

title: Age Twisters is a simple yet charming spin on the co-op adventure that aims to feel like watching a Pixar movie
summary: The puzzles won't stump you, but Piccolo Studios says they're not supposed to.
body: As I'm making my way through the beginning of two-player co-op adventure Age Twisters alongside the founders of developer Piccolo Studios, I'm told the goal was to create a game that evokes the same feelings as watching a Pixar movie with your child. Now I am admittedly sprogless, but it wasn't difficult to latch onto those similar fuzzy feelings of nostalgia and familial love even as I completed puzzles alongside a man I'd only met minutes prior. Age Twisters is the studio's attempt at a game like It Takes Two or Split Fiction, albeit much lower on the toughness scale—something which the developer itself admits, instead going for a game that's constantly evolving and different rather than outright difficult. It takes a granddaughter-grandfather duo and slaps a couple of age-bending bracelets on them, allowing each one to age up or down all the way from a young child to a hobbling old bean. (Image credit: Krafton) It's a wonderfully novel mechanic—each age has its own portrait, voice acting, and dynamic dialogue that'll shift as you age up or down across the story. title: Arc Raiders' executive producer admits its developers 'couldn't keep pace with the players' and their need for content, but promises Frozen Trail as the answer
summary: "What we want to do is spend more time building quality stuff."
body: If there's one thing you should never underestimate, it's a gamer's love for completing little tasks. Whether it's battle passes, meaningless fetch quests, or in Arc Raiders' case, its expeditions. There's just the right amount of dopamine involved for a neuron activation, so you best bet that they'll rip through them at an unthinkable speed. I'll concede that Embark Studios probably couldn't have foreseen the full extent of this love prior to Arc Raiders release, but still, the outcome is the same: gamers out-growing their once-beloved game because they managed to complete all their tasks way too fast. (Image credit: Embark) "We didn’t really expect that amount of players to show up and play ARC Raiders," executive producer Aleksander Grøndal explains in an interview with GamesBeat . "That surprised us. We were a bit unprepared. That’s one of the hard lessons we had to learn. When January came and some of the problems started with the game." January saw the first crack in Arc Raiders' armour, as the novelty began to wear off and players became more keenly aware of how limited its content was alongside growing concerns about cheating and stream sniping . title: Nvidia puts its money where its mouth is on open weight AI, moving to buy Hugging Face for $13 billion
summary: Come on guys, fling a few mil my way?
body: Nvidia has just announced that it intends to acquire Hugging Face, the biggest open platform dedicated to developing machine-learning applications. Considering Nvidia has been all-in on AI for the past few years—to the point that I barely remember the last time the company even mentioned gaming in an earnings call—it's hardly a surprising move. What did encourage a sharp intake of breath from me though was the price of this purchase; Nvidia will buy Hugging Face for a total of $12,930,300,000 . $11.9 billion of that will go to Hugging Face's investors, while employees that join Nvidia will be offered an ‌equity-based retention ⁠program of up to $1 billion, according to Reuters . But even though there's billions of dollars in the mix, that doesn't mean the walls are about to come down around Hugging Face. "Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem," Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang writes, "Developers will choose the models they want, the frameworks they want, the clouds and inference service providers they want and the computing platforms they want.
